assessment.headline: DAY 36. Green Sanvi crosses — India's lifeline holds. But F-15 crew missing, April 6 tomorrow, and the world has no plan for Hormuz.
assessment.body:
Two narratives compete today:

THE GOOD: Green Sanvi crossed the Strait of Hormuz with 46,650 MT of LPG, becoming the 9th Indian carrier (7th LPG tanker) to transit safely. Indian warship confirmed escorting. It reaches Mumbai by April 6. Green Asha and Jag Vikram are next. Six smaller Indian cargo ships are also moving through Oman's waters. India's Hormuz pipeline is WORKING — diplomacy + Navy escort delivering results.

THE BAD: An F-15E crew member is missing in Iran for a second day. Iran offered a $60,000 bounty. Two Black Hawk rescue helicopters were also hit. The UN Hormuz vote was postponed AGAIN — Russia, China, and France still oppose. Trump reversed himself — now says 'OPEN THE STRAIT, TAKE THE OIL, MAKE A FORTUNE' after saying 'countries do it themselves' just 2 days ago. Kuwait's desalination plant was hit. Iran targeted Oracle's Dubai office and named 18 US tech companies.

For India (Day 36, 7:15 PM):
• Green Sanvi: 46,650 MT LPG reaching Mumbai Apr 6 — positive
• 17 Indian ships east of Hormuz (460 seafarers). 9 carriers crossed total
• Green Asha + Jag Vikram confirmed next (IANS)
• 6 cargo ships moving via Oman waters (MSV Al Shirazi, Faizane Mustafa etc.)
• USA overtook UAE as India's #1 LPG supplier
• 60 days fuel stock. LPG 30+ days. Refineries >100%
• India supplying fuel to 5 neighbors
• BW Elm rerouted to Ennore (arriving Apr 4)

APRIL 6 = TOMORROW:
• If deadline passes with no deal: power plant strikes begin
• If F-15 crew found alive by Iran: POW crisis extends war
• If F-15 crew found dead: domestic political pressure to escalate
• Monday: Indian markets reopen into all of this

The Green Sanvi crossing is the best news India has had all week. But 36 days into the war, the world still has no plan to reopen Hormuz — and the man who started the war just said he wants to 'take the oil.'
